text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: elevated 5xx and timeouts observed for /v1/generate (prod) — severity: high — page delivered to oncall
alice (oncall): I see errors spiking in Datadog, 502/504 gateway timeouts across multiple regions. Noted increased queue depth on batching scheduler.
raj: Confirmed. Error rate up ~12% over last 5m, p90 latency creeping past 2s then timing out. Logs show "batcher: enqueue_time" backlog.
carla: Any customer-facing outages? CS reporting increased failed requests for a few enterprise customers.
customer-success: We're getting tickets from two clients about 500s and slow responses. They're seeing retries.
alice (oncall): Starting live triage. What changed in last deploy window?
mike: No new deploys to runtime in the last 24h. Autoscaler rolled a few workers earlier but that should help.
raj: Metrics: scheduler queue depth jumped from ~200 to ~25k across pool-A in 10m. Head-of-line blocking suspected: long-running large-context requests sitting at front.
oncall-ml: Possible thundering-herd on long-context retokenizations + cache misses. Also seeing KV-cache eviction thrashing.
sre-rotation: Can we get a quick dump of the oldest queue entries and example request sizes?
alice (oncall): Grabbed a sample. Showing many requests with seq_len 8192 and model_variant=huge-quant.
carla: That would explain slow per-request generation time — huge-quant on small GPU pool.
raj: Also see lots of small requests blocked behind those large ones (classic HOL). 5xx appear when the gateway hits proxy timeout waiting for a backend response.
infra-bot: Autoscale events: +0 nodes (scale suppressed due to capacity cap), pool-A GPUs at 96% memory, 98% compute.
alice (oncall): Immediate mitigations brainstorm: (1) route new traffic to fallback model variant (smaller quant) (2) enable per-request priority preemption or evict long-waiting small requests to fast path (3) temporarily increase gateway timeout? Any risks?
mike: Increasing gateway timeout just delays failures — better to reduce head-of-line by moving small requests off the blocked queue.
raj: We have a canary route to model-compact-1 that is compatible. I recommend switching non-enterprise traffic to compact.
carla: For enterprise customers with dedicated SLAs, we need explicit opt-in before switching their model. Customer-success, can you confirm which customers are impacted?
customer-success: Two enterprise accounts impacted: AcmeCorp and NovaApps. AcmeCorp is high severity. We should avoid changing their model without approval.
ops-lead: Do safe fallback for the rest of traffic, and for impacted enterprises start phone outreach.
alice (oncall): Action list: 1) Raj -> move public route /v1/generate default to model-compact-1 (traffic cutover) 2) Mike -> enable aggressive queue eviction for requests older than 10s (non-enterprise) 3) Carla -> open support case/inform AcmeCorp and NovaApps 4) SRE -> monitor error-rate and gateway 502/504 delta.
raj: Starting rollout to route-default -> model-compact-1 now. Will keep canary at 5% for 2m then ramp.
raj: Canaries OK at 5%... 25%... ramping to 100% for non-enterprise.
alice (oncall): Mike, what's the command to enable eviction?
mike: Running: ```./adminctl scheduler set-eviction --age=10s --scope=non-enterprise``` 
mike: Eviction flag flipped. Purging long-waiting small ones as they surface.
infra-bot: Eviction jobs: purged 3,421 queued requests older than 10s from pool-A.
raj: Observability update: queue depth dropping from 25k -> 3.8k, p95 latency improving.
carla: Reached AcmeCorp on phone, they acknowledged and agreed to a temporary fallback if needed.
customer-success: NovaApps prefers manual approval; we're working it.
alice (oncall): We need to avoid evicting enterprise customer requests — ensure filter respected.
mike: Eviction scope verified: non-enterprise only.
sre-rotation: Error-rate trending down: 5xx from 12% -> 3.2% in 10m. Gateway timeouts also decreasing.
raj: Still seeing a small cluster of long runners causing intermittent 502s in region-eu-west. I'm going to temporarily drain that worker and restart the batcher process.
raj: `kubectl drain node/gpu-eu-23 && kubectl delete pod batcher-xyz`
infra-bot: Node drain started for gpu-eu-23. Pod batcher-xyz terminated and restarted on gpu-eu-45.
raj: After restart, that node's local cache warmed slower but no more >60s requests from it. Removing a big HOL offender.
alice (oncall): Good. What's current customer impact?
customer-success: AcmeCorp saw ~40 failed requests during peak; most recovered. We'll follow up for an incident report. NovaApps still reported some timeouts but at lower rates.
ops-lead: Recommend temporary capacity cap increase for pool-A to avoid suppression during incident window. Need approval.
alice (oncall): I'll request it now.
alice (oncall): Request sent to finance/infra leads.
infra-bot: Capacity cap increase approved: pool-A max nodes +4 for 2h. Scaling up now.
raj: New nodes coming up, queue depth continues to fall.
carla: Any permanent fixes? Root causes so far: (a) large-context heavy requests landing on the same batcher pool, (b) KV-cache thrash causing stalls, (c) autoscale cap prevented quick scale up.
oncall-ml: Longer-term: add request scoring to batcher to avoid mixing long-context requests with short ones; enforce per-request size routing to different pools. Also improve cache warming for migrated pods.
sre-rotation: We'll schedule a follow-up P0 with engineering to add preemption and per-size queues.
alice (oncall): Post-incident items: - Postmortem doc - add feature: per-size routing + batcher preemption - add dashboard alert for queue depth per pool (threshold: 2k) - revisit capacity cap heuristics
carla: Creating incident doc and inviting owners.
customer-success: I'll prepare customer-facing summary for AcmeCorp and NovaApps.
alice (oncall): Status: mitigated. Error rates back to baseline. Keeping incident channel open for 1h for observation.
incident-bot: Incident severity downgraded to medium; ongoing monitoring for 1h.
ops-lead: Thanks team. We'll reconvene for postmortem tomorrow 11:00 UTC.
carla: Noted. Adding notes to the incident board.
alice (oncall): Thanks everyone. Closing active mitigations but leaving notes and follow-ups.
